newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First's popularity slumps in TVNZ poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ First's popularity slumps in TVNZ poll.

text.p: The New Zealand First Party's popularity has slipped to just seven percent, almost half that of election night last October, according to a TVNZ-Colmar Brunton opinion poll released on Tuesday.
NZ First's showing was the lowest since 1995.
TVNZ said the National Party's rating went up nine points to 45 percent while Labour gained three to 31 percent.
TVNZ said support for the Alliance dropped three points to seven percent while ACT New Zealand dropped to four percent.
Translated into seats, the poll showed National would gain 56 seats and NZ First nine, giving the coalition 65 seats -- four more than it has now.
Labour would have 40, the Alliance nine and ACT six.
Treasurer and NZ First Leader Winston Peters' personal popularity fell to six percent, its lowest point since July 1995.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger's popularity firmed five to 28, and Labour Leader Helen Clark gained two to 19 while the Alliance's Jim Anderton slipped six to five percent.
Just 25 percent approved of National-NZ First coalition's performance, TVNZ said.
